case_name: Sri V Nandakumar S/O G Vaidyalingam vs Smt M Indumathi W/O V Nandakumar

parties.respondent_defendant: M Indumathi W/O V Nandakumar, wife

facts_of_case: Husband and wife are parties. Husband filed petition for divorce under Hindu Marriage Act. Trial court awarded interim maintenance to wife.

legal_principles.principle: The Court must consider the object with which the Act is enacted and not just the literal words.
legal_principles.held: There cannot be any doubt as to the object of a proceeding for maintenance, it is to provide food and shelter to the deserted wife.

legal_principles.principle: The Court must consider the socio-economic aspect of a case and not just the legal duty.
legal_principles.held: The real object is to provide food and shelter to the deserted wife, and provision enables the Court to see that the spouse is put in a financial hell.

legal_principles.principle: The Court must consider the financial hardship of a spouse and not just the legal obligation.
legal_principles.held: The trial Court must have passed an order in favour of the wife to see that she maintains herself and her child.

use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for divorce under Hindu Marriage Act
quashing an order in a family court case
advising on the relevance of Article 226 in a writ petition
